heading: IOI head roles recur, but a shared circuit across models remains contested
definition: circuits with the same head classes and roles carry IOI in other models, sizes and training checkpoints, and their components are reused for other tasks.
summary: Independent studies report recurring IOI head roles and reuse of circuit components on other tasks, but a shared complete circuit across models and training stages remains contested. Removing heads proposed to copy names into the output can improve IOI, and some heads that suppress signals in the mature model show little effect early in training.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: R2 for selected roles and post-emergence structure; C for persistence of the mature-selected suppressing computation at early GPT-2 checkpoints. 1-10B: C for invariant head classes and roles; R2 for selected functional correspondences. Toy: an alternative symbolic circuit is reported, but counts do not provide a separate toy bucket. 10-100B and >100B: ?; no coverage in the supplied size counts.
suggested_status.reason: The full wording is contested by causal screen tests: arXiv:2606.05378#R3 and arXiv:2606.05378#R21 show improved Pythia-1B IOI after removing purported mover or late-layer groups. Early-checkpoint evidence also warrants challenges: replacing future mature suppressor L10H10 in alias-gpt2-small-x21 at step 1500 changes logit difference by about −0.002 (arXiv:2610.04119#R39); replacing future mature suppressor L10H7 in battlestar-gpt2-small-x49 at step 1500 likewise changes it by about −0.002 (arXiv:2610.04119#R43). These results indicate absence of the mature-selected suppressing computation in these early conditions; they do not exclude other early suppressors. Bounded recurrence is supported by Pythia checkpoint path patching (arXiv:2407.10827#R1–R13), multilingual BLOOM role analysis (arXiv:2410.09223#r3–r4), and mature suppressor interventions (arXiv:2610.04119#R20–R22). These do not establish an invariant complete circuit. Supplied pre-check counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies=16; versions.V3.verdicts.challenges.studies=1. These counts do not incorporate the checker's early-checkpoint reclassification. versions.V3.studies_by_size contains <1B and 1-10B but no larger stated-size buckets. The author-overlap count, versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=2, is aggregate and does not identify which headers it applies to.
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched comparison using the same prompts, causal role definitions, ablation controls and metrics could determine whether divergent screened-head effects reflect different circuits or different candidate selection. Complete role maps across capable model families, seeds, early-to-mature checkpoints and larger scales would change the scope assessment. Causal cross-task tests in non-GPT-2 models would strengthen the reuse clause.

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.setup: The original study preliminarily examined which GPT-2 medium heads directly influenced IOI logits.
original_result.result: A sparse set of heads directly influenced the logits. These heads did not all attend to the indirect object and subject.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: GPT2-Medium recovers indirect object identification (IOI) head classes and reuses several components for Colored Objects.
IOI copy suppression generalizes to OpenWebText, correlating across model classes with suppression of repeated continuations.
Parameter analysis classifies all GPT-2 medium IOI mover heads as name copying.
Pythia IOI circuit roles remain stable across tested sizes after circuit formation.
BLOOM preserves IOI functions across languages, and CPM reproduces suppression of the subject’s name.
Pythia reproduces suppression signals to name-copying heads; GPT-2 reuses suppression for retrieving items (Laundry List).
GPT-2 small reuses IOI heads in syllogism circuits.
GPT-2-small retains a recognizable IOI pathway after tokenizer permutation.
Clean IOI fine-tuning preserves GPT-2-small's head classes across tested checkpoints.
One Pythia head develops name-mover-like attention when IOI emerges.
Name-mover ablation substantially reduces OLMoE IOI accuracy.
Pythia-1B and LLaMA-3.2-1B have causally important, attention-dominated IOI circuits.
Repeated-name suppression recurs across mature Pythia models and independent GPT-2 Small runs.
GPT-2 small's duplicate-token heads, including an IOI head, recognize repetitions beyond names.
GPT-2 small's negative name mover performs copy suppression across its training distribution.
Larger models retain sender roles that causally steer name-mover attention.
IOI component reuse varies across tasks, and larger GPT2 models show reduced head overlap.
Copy suppression is weaker in Pythia than in GPT-2.
Mamba routes IOI through a convolutional and state-space bottleneck.
Pythia changes copy-suppression contributions, and Pythia-160m lacks duplicate-token heads.
CPM replaces negative name movers with a differently routed copy-suppression head.
The reused suppression signal has limited capacity to retrieve items by position from longer Laundry Lists.
Reused GPT-2 IOI heads change their contributions across syllogism tasks.
A small attention-only model solves symbolic IOI with additive and contrastive heads.
Tokenizer permutation changes individual IOI head roles despite preserving the broader pathway.
IOI fine-tuning recruits additional heads and shifts a backup head into name moving.
Llama-3.2-1B shows late mover-like and inhibitor-like heads without causal role validation.
Cross-task IOI circuit overlap largely reflects general-purpose MLPs and shrinks at neuron resolution.
IOI head classes have different causal importance across Pythia, OLMo and OLMoE.
Pythia-14M IOI circuits show no significant contribution beyond random subgraphs.
Heads that become mature suppressors later in training contribute negligibly during early training.
DistilGPT-2 fails IOI and shows little preservation of GPT-2's circuit.
Larger-model sender roles correspond less closely, and name-mover rewrites remain incomplete.
Several screened IOI head classes prove dispensable or harmful across tested architectures.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Preservation of the original head classes and roles at model scales above 10B.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size has <1B, 1-10B and not stated, with no 10-100B or >100B entries. The larger-model role evidence remains preliminary or topology-only: arXiv:2310.08744#r15 and arXiv:2512.10903#ioi-llama-8b-structure.

untested.what: Complete original-class decompositions in the larger Pythia checkpoints omitted from circuit finding; mappings beyond the selected Pythia inhibition–mover interaction; and complete causal head-class mappings in the Llama pruning and larger GPT-2 analyses.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_family and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation show family coverage but do not encode complete role identification. arXiv:2407.10827 explicitly leaves Pythia-6.9b and 12b circuits untested. Within the selected-component analysis, arXiv:2406.09519#R13 observes Pythia-160m inhibition head 6.6 communicating with mover 9.5; remaining classes are untested there. arXiv:2512.10903#ioi-llama-1b-roles identifies analogous late-layer roles through attention/DLA without complete class mapping or causal role tests; arXiv:2512.10903#ioi-llama-1b-structure retains two layer-2 heads, so early classes are not demonstrated absent. Llama-3.1-8B and GPT-2-XL have topology without named-role mappings in arXiv:2512.10903#ioi-llama-8b-structure and arXiv:2512.10903#ioi-gpt2xl-topology. The preliminary GPT2-Large/XL analysis arXiv:2310.08744#r15 leaves upstream classes unanalysed.

untested.what: Causal, role-preserving reuse of identified IOI head classes on other tasks in non-GPT-2 families.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.addition.by_family contains only GPT-2. Cross-family task overlap in arXiv:2605.08348#r1 does not identify preserved IOI head classes or roles: state=cannot_determine for Gemma 2, Llama 3.2 and Qwen3 under EAP-IG and relevance patching, K=10%, P=50%. General-purpose shared machinery is a preliminary interpretation; detailed shared-core analysis is restricted to Llama-3.2-3B. arXiv:2310.04625#r14 is a score association. No causal role-preserving cross-task reuse test is reported in arXiv:2407.10827; this omission is not explicitly identified as future work. The multilingual study arXiv:2410.09223 leaves task reuse untested.

untested.what: Preservation of a complete, causally validated IOI head-class decomposition through instruction or reasoning post-training.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_stage and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation contain instruct/chat and reasoning entries, so those stages are not wholly untested. However, arXiv:2605.08348#r1 measures generic overlap, and the complete-role mapping is not supplied. The explicit checkpoint-class preservation result in arXiv:2503.01896#R1\u2013R7 concerns clean-IOI fine-tuning.

untested.what: Complete original head-class and role mappings for the circuits examined through whole-circuit contributions and the illustrative Pythia emergence result.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation records measurement, patching and removal coverage but does not establish complete class mappings. arXiv:2605.21303#R2 and arXiv:2605.21303#R3 report positive whole-circuit contributions in Pythia-1B and LLaMA-3.2-1B EAP-IG IOI circuits; they provide partial V3 support without identifying the original classes and roles. arXiv:2606.25010#R2 shows a selected Pythia head becoming roughly name-mover-like on one canonical prompt; other classes and task reuse remain untested. Its model size, seed, checkpoint, layer and head index are unspecified.

untested.what: Functional analogues of the named GPT-2 duplicate-token, S-inhibition and name-mover roles in attention-free Mamba.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_family and versions.V3.coverage_by_operation include Mamba, but the checker reclassifies arXiv:2407.14008 as cites_only with no V3 verdict. arXiv:2407.14008#R1, arXiv:2407.14008#R3, arXiv:2407.14008#R4, arXiv:2407.14008#R8 and arXiv:2407.14008#R9 concern Mamba-370m layer-level mechanisms, including a layer-39 convolution/SSM bottleneck and layers 0 and 15. They supply no mapping or test of the named GPT-2 roles; these results provide coverage rather than negative V3 evidence.

wording_issues.phrase: the same head classes and roles
wording_issues.issue: Class membership and role sign vary: Pythia-160m lacks duplicate-token heads, Pythia copy suppression changes sign relative to GPT-2, and CPM replaces negative movers with a differently routed suppressor.

The statement needs a model and capability condition. DistilGPT-2 does not perform IOI successfully on the tested clean prompts; a task-trained symbolic attention-only toy model solves IOI through additive and contrastive heads under rigid BABA/BAAB sequences.

Pythia stability is reported after circuit formation. At step 1500, replacing future mature suppressor L10H10 in alias-gpt2-small-x21 (native logit difference −1.475) or L10H7 in battlestar-gpt2-small-x49 (native logit difference −1.741) changes logit difference by about −0.002 in each run. These early results challenge persistence of the mature-selected suppressing function across checkpoints; they do not exclude other early suppressors.

wording_issues.phrase: the same head classes and roles
wording_issues.issue: Candidate selection by attention-pattern similarity does not ensure the predicted causal role. In Pythia-1B, ablating screened name movers helps IOI; in OLMoE, screened S-inhibition affects the logit margin without materially changing top-1 accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Overlap threshold, task and model size
method_sensitivity.what: GPT2-Medium's 25/32 shared-head result uses the top-2% importance threshold. Preliminary top-10 overlap is 5/10 in GPT2-Large and 0/10 in GPT2-XL. These are different overlap definitions and model conditions, not a matched replication disagreement.

On Colored Objects, forcing an IOI inhibition signal produces predicted mover responses even though the unmodified task uses content gatherers and its inhibition signal slightly hurts. On GPT-2-small Laundry List, the intervention's effectiveness depends on object count and the selected component's expressivity: a single component tends to select the first or last candidate. With 8 objects, answer-index-conditioned intervention accuracy is about 51%; a numeric unmodified 8-object baseline is not stated. These indexing-capacity limits retain component reuse and do not establish a V3 scope limitation.

method_sensitivity.factor: Head-selection screen, intervention target and metric
method_sensitivity.what: Pythia-1B screened name-mover ablation improves top-1 accuracy, while whole EAP-IG circuit ablation has positive ΔT and mature suppressor replacement reduces logit difference. These select different components and use different measures. The EAP-IG result is partial evidence for V3: positive whole-circuit contribution does not establish the original head classes and roles. Within the screened-head study, union ablation differs from individual classes, and OLMoE S-inhibition changes margin without a corresponding top-1 loss.

For IOI task circuits in Gemma 2, Llama 3.2 and Qwen3 at K=10%, P=50%, automated component-level circuits overlap other tasks strongly, while neuron-level circuits barely overlap. The study also reports low same-task overlap between EAP-IG and relevance patching. Measured component sharing depends on discovery method and unit of analysis. General-purpose shared machinery is a preliminary interpretation; the detailed shared-core analysis is restricted to Llama-3.2-3B. Identified IOI head classes and roles are not tracked, so preservation and role-preserving reuse are cannot_determine for V3; these overlap results do not establish a V3 scope limitation.

Pythia role stability is conditional on post-emergence checkpoints. At step 1500, replacement of future mature suppressor L10H10 in alias-gpt2-small-x21 changes logit difference by about −0.002, with native baseline −1.475; future mature suppressor L10H7 in battlestar-gpt2-small-x49 likewise has an effect about −0.002, with native baseline −1.741. Their mature effects are substantial. These early results challenge recurrence of the mature-selected suppressing function at those checkpoints; other early suppressors remain possible. Clean-IOI fine-tuning preserves functional classes despite changing head assignments, supporting V3 without requiring identical head indices.

The obfuscated-model study describes broad similarity through logit attribution but redistributed or inconsistent roles through component and head patching. MAPS classifies all retained GPT-2-medium Mover heads as implementing name copying, without testing their causal IOI role. Previously labeled movers 14.5, 17.10, 16.0, 18.12 and 21.7 were excluded from counting because the authors considered their prior justification insufficient.

Role-directed sender rewrites are more effective than arbitrary sender resampling in the input-swap-graph comparison: the resampling curve lies above the rewrite curve for IO-minus-S logit difference. This makes the intervention's semantic content relevant to judging role correspondence.

method_sensitivity.factor: Task format for a reused head
method_sensitivity.what: For GPT-2 small, full-model average logit difference is 1.8575 on Simple Syllogism and 1.2123 on Opposite Syllogism, each over 500 prompts. Mean-ablating head 10.7 improves Simple Syllogism performance beyond baseline; its direct-effect path patching reduces Opposite Syllogism logit difference. Neither head-specific change is numerically stated. These results support component reuse under V3 despite the changed contribution sign; V3 does not require invariant roles across non-IOI tasks.
